scheme_name: Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
description:
The Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Maharashtra in India.

This scheme was launched on 1st January 2021.

It aims to provide financial assistance to workers in the unorganized sector who are facing serious health issues.

The primary objective of the scheme is to offer medical assistance to laborers who are unable to work due to severe illnesses.

The scheme specifically targets the following groups: Theka Shramik (contract workers), Hamaal Shramik (porters), and Gharelu Mahila Kamgar (domestic workers).

Eligible beneficiaries can receive financial assistance of up to INR 1 lakh for medical treatment.

The scheme also aims to alleviate the financial burden on these workers and their families during critical health situations.

To qualify for the benefits under this scheme, applicants must be aged between 18 and 60 years.

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 1 lakh per annum for individuals.

Applicants must be registered under the Maharashtra Labour Welfare Board to avail of the benefits.

The application process involves several steps that must be followed accurately.

Firstly, applicants need to fill out the application form available at the local Labour Welfare Board offices.

Secondly, they must provide necessary documents such as proof of identity, proof of income, and medical certificates.

The application must be submitted along with these documents to the nearest Labour Welfare Board office.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the designated officials.

The review process typically takes about 15 days.

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account.

The scheme is designed to provide timely support to individuals facing health crises.

The financial assistance can be utilized for various medical expenses including hospitalization, surgeries, and medication.

The disbursement of funds is generally processed within 30 days of application approval.

The Maharashtra Labour Welfare Board is the implementing authority for this scheme.

The Board operates under the Department of Labour, Government of Maharashtra.

For any inquiries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the Maharashtra Labour Welfare Board at their official helpline number 1800 233 3330.

The scheme is part of the broader initiative by the Maharashtra government to support unorganized sector workers.

It recognizes the vulnerability of these workers in times of health emergencies.

The initiative is also aligned with the national goal of improving healthcare access for marginalized communities.

The scheme has been well-received, with thousands of applications processed since its inception.

In the first year alone, over 10,000 beneficiaries received financial assistance under this scheme.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the financial year 2021-2022.

This allocation is aimed at ensuring that sufficient funds are available to meet the healthcare needs of eligible workers.

The scheme is expected to expand in the coming years to include more beneficiaries.

It is also anticipated that the income limit may be revised to accommodate more workers.

The Maharashtra government is committed to enhancing the welfare of laborers through various initiatives.

The Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana is a significant step in this direction.

The scheme reflects the government's recognition of the essential role played by unorganized sector workers in the economy.

It also emphasizes the need for social security measures for these workers.

The scheme is part of a larger framework of labor reforms being implemented in Maharashtra.

These reforms aim to create a more supportive environment for workers in the unorganized sector.

The government is also working on awareness campaigns to inform potential beneficiaries about the scheme.

Such campaigns are crucial for ensuring that eligible workers are aware of their rights and available benefits.

The Maharashtra Labour Welfare Board is actively engaging with local communities to promote the scheme.

This engagement includes organizing workshops and informational sessions.

The scheme is expected to contribute to improved health outcomes for workers in the unorganized sector.

By providing financial assistance, the government aims to reduce the incidence of medical debt among these workers.

The Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana represents a proactive approach to labor welfare.

It is a testament to the government's commitment to social justice and equity.

The scheme is a vital resource for those who may not have access to traditional health insurance.

It is designed to fill the gaps in healthcare access for the most vulnerable populations.

The government is continuously monitoring the implementation of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness.

Feedback from beneficiaries is being collected to make necessary adjustments.

The Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana is an essential part of Maharashtra's welfare landscape.

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other states across India.

The scheme is a clear indication of the government's recognition of the challenges faced by unorganized sector workers.

It aims to empower these workers by providing them with the necessary support during health crises.

The Maharashtra government is dedicated to improving the quality of life for all its citizens.

Through this scheme, it is taking significant steps toward achieving that goal.
